inventory.docstring: Convert a scalar or array between two units of the same dimension.
Convert to the internal SI base unit of the unit's dimension.

Total stress, pore pressure and effective stress [kPa] at depth(s) z [m].

Soil above ``gwt_depth`` uses ``gamma``; below it uses ``gamma_sat``.
Pore pressure is hydrostatic from the groundwater table.
Returns floats for scalar z, otherwise numpy arrays.
C_R by rod length [m] (Youd et al. 2001, Table 2).
C_S: 1.0 for a standard sampler; 1.1-1.3 for a sampler without liners.
C_N = (Pa / sigma'_v0)^0.5 <= 1.7 (Liao & Whitman 1986; NCEER cap).

Apply energy, equipment and overburden corrections to all SPT records.

Rod length is taken as test depth + ``rod_stickup`` (length above ground) [m].
q_t = q_c + u2 (1 - a). Without u2, q_t = q_c.
n = 0.381 I_c + 0.05 (sigma'_v0 / Pa) - 0.15, limited to <= 1.0 (Robertson 2009).

Solve Q_tn, n and I_c simultaneously (Robertson 2009).

Returns (Qtn, Fr, Ic, n, converged) as arrays; invalid points (q_t <= sigma_v0,
sigma'_v0 <= 0 or f_s <= 0, where I_c is undefined) are NaN and count as converged.
Integrate a unit-weight log: sigma_v by trapezoids from the surface, hydrostatic u.

Process a CPT sounding.

Stresses come from ``profile`` when given; otherwise unit weight is estimated from the
CPT itself (Robertson & Cabal 2010) and ``gwt_depth`` (or the sounding's own GWT) is used.
A-line: PI = 0.73 (LL - 20).
U-line (upper bound of natural soils): PI = 0.9 (LL - 8).
Plasticity class of fines: 'C', 'M' or 'CL-ML' (hatched zone).
I_c = sqrt((3.47 - log Qtn)^2 + (log Fr + 1.22)^2).
Invert I_c on the log10(Qtn) <= 3.47 branch; undefined points are NaN.
Return the existing sensitive-soil boundary Qtn = 12 exp(-1.4 Fr).
Zones 2-7 from I_c (Robertson 2009/2010). NaN I_c gives zone 0 (undefined).

SBTn zone 1-9 (0 where undefined).

Zone 1 is assigned where Qtn < 12 exp(-1.4 Fr) (Robertson 2010).

Zones 8 and 9 use the Robertson (2010) boundary
Qtn > 1 / (0.005 (Fr - 1) - 0.0003 (Fr - 1)^2 - 0.002), with 1.5 < Fr <= 4.5 for zone 8
and Fr > 4.5 for zone 9. These boundary equations are pending verification against the
source (Phase 0), so they are disabled by default.
Sand-like (drained, potentially liquefiable) behaviour for I_c < 2.6.

Convert a proposal without selecting or approving design parameters.

``gamma`` uses zero-based layer indices and supplies both unit weights when
a suggestion is unavailable. Suggested weights take precedence; gamma_sat
follows SoilLayer's existing convention when not supplied.

Preserve log layers, absorbing unlogged gaps into the layer above.

Tests at shared boundaries belong to the lower interval (SoilProfile convention);
a test at the final log bottom belongs to the final interval. Finite non-refusal
N60 alone contributes to means. All-refusal means are None: ResultNumber is
float | None (api/schemas.py), with no lower-bound field. The first layer is
extended to ground surface; all extensions are warned. Tests and means use
the resulting contiguous intervals; tests below the final bottom are warned.
Adjacent tops within Borehole's DEPTH_TOL are snapped to the previous bottom;
intervals with non-positive thickness after snapping are dropped and warned
before assigning tests. The final retained interval includes its bottom test.
``processed=None`` is permitted only for a borehole with no SPT tests.

Split when the lab group changes or relative corrected N60 change exceeds settings.

N_i and the current mean are finite corrected N60 observations. A zero mean
followed by positive N starts a new segment; zero followed by zero does not.
Missing N is ignored for comparison/statistics, with a warning. Missing USCS
remains None and is a distinct group, never filled from a distant sample.
Minimum-thickness merging processes the thinnest segment (tie: upper), and
prefers the same USCS group, then the closest finite N60 mean; undefined
distances and ties select the upper neighbour. Mixed merged
groups retain the dominant known group by midpoint-cell thickness, then sample
count, then uppermost occurrence, with uscs_mixed. Behaviour remains provisional
and warned. Refusal values are excluded from comparisons and means; all-refusal
means are None (ResultNumber supports null, not a lower bound). All means are
sample-weighted, not means of segment means. Settings are algorithm choices,
not empirical soil thresholds.
An unapproved interpretation; fields map directly to ProposedLayer.
Fields map directly to LayeringProposal without importing the HTTP package.
Half-open sample indices; geometry comes from midpoint cell edges.
Validate aligned 1-D samples, stable-sort depths, and reject duplicate depths.

Start at ground surface, as SoilProfile requires; end at the last data depth.

Internal edges are arithmetic midpoints, an algorithmic interpretation rather
than a published soil threshold. A sole sample at zero has no positive extent.
Callers use warn_no_data to disclose unsupported extensions and local gaps.
Arithmetic mean of finite observations; missing observations are not zero.
Append a warning using the shared format and named SI-depth context.

Flag extrapolation and gaps exceeding adjacent local sample spacing.

Local spacing is the minimum of the available neighbouring acquisition
increments: comparison with the smaller neighbour reports an interruption
even when sampling density changes on the other side. This is an algorithmic
reporting rule, not a soil property or a geological threshold. Discarded
observations also supply spacing evidence. With only two original observations
there is no independent reference spacing, so even a large separation cannot
be reported as an internal gap; surface/trailing extensions are still flagged.
DEPTH_TOL is only the existing numerical depth tolerance, not a geological
gap threshold.

Merge the thinnest eligible segment first (equal thickness: upper).

The most similar adjacent segment wins; equal distances choose the upper
neighbour. A single segment is retained even when the record is thinner than
the user setting. No geological coefficient is introduced.
Copy settings and deduplicate identical warning messages in occurrence order.

Propose layers from processed Ic; never mutate the input or approve values.

A centred window of total depth width ``smoothing_window`` includes both
endpoints and averages finite samples with equal weight (not a sample-count
window). Non-finite Ic samples are omitted with a warning; the original final
depth is retained. Midpoints of retained samples define internal boundaries.
Contiguous smoothed zones are merged thinnest first (tie: upper) for minimum
thickness, then for strict |mean Ic difference| < ``merge_ic_tol``.
Ties select the upper neighbour;
tolerance scanning restarts at the top after each merge. Layer statistics and
merge distances use original, unsmoothed Ic observations, not averages of means.
A mean-Ic zone can differ from individual members' zones. Upstream exceptional
sbtn_zone zones 1/8/9 are protected from smoothing and both merge passes.
Zone 1 provisionally uses undrained behaviour because Robertson ZONE_NAMES
identifies it as sensitive, fine grained. Zones 8/9 use is_sand_like on the
layer mean Ic: their exceptional zone number alone supplies no drainage rule.
All exceptional behaviours carry behaviour_assumed for engineer review.
Every proposal warns that the Ic < 2.6 criterion (Robertson 2009) alone does
not establish drainage for the loading case; straddling layers also warn.
Every raw-zone run differing from its final layer zone is reported, including
single samples; discarded samples break runs. At most one lens_smoothed
warning per final layer lists its runs (observed depth ranges and raw zones).

gamma_suggested is the mean of the existing registered RC2010_gamma_CPT
correlation evaluated at each retained observation: Robertson & Cabal (2010),
gamma/gamma_w = 0.27 log10(Rf) + 0.36 log10(qt/Pa) + 1.236.
Its existing numerical Rf floor is reused unchanged. Non-positive/non-finite
qt or negative/non-finite fs are excluded, with a warning; gamma uses the
remaining valid estimates. No SBT zone i18n key exists in geotek/i18n/tr.json,
so descriptions are left empty for the engineer/UI.
E / Pa = alpha N60.
E' = alpha_E (q_t - sigma_v0), alpha_E = 0.015 * 10^(0.55 I_c + 1.68).
Correlations for ``parameter`` whose required inputs are all available.

Evaluate one correlation at a point. Extra keys in ``inputs`` act as context for checks
(e.g. ``Ic`` to flag a sand correlation used in clay).

Mean of several correlation results, with min/mean/max spread.

With ``only_valid`` results outside their validity range are excluded; if none remain,
all results are used and the combined value is flagged invalid.
Warn when input or option ``name`` lies outside [low, high].
tan phi' = (1/2.68) [log(q_c / sigma'_v0) + 0.29].
sin phi' = 0.8 - 0.094 ln(PI).
s_u = (q_t - sigma_v0) / N_kt.
s_u = (u2 - u0) / N_du.
s_u = f1 N60.
True where the raw Robertson & Cabal estimate is finite and below GAMMA_MIN_RC2010.

gamma / gamma_w = 0.27 log R_f + 0.36 log(q_t/Pa) + 1.236, R_f = f_s/q_t * 100 [%],
floored at GAMMA_MIN_RC2010 (NaN stays NaN; callers warn via ``rc2010_below_floor``).
D_r = sqrt((N1)60 / C_d), in percent.
sigma'_p = k (q_t - sigma_v0).
FC = 80 (I_c + C_FC) - 137, limited to 0-100 %.
r_d = exp[alpha(z) + beta(z) M]; NaN below 34 m.
K_sigma = 1 - C_sigma ln(sigma'_v0 / Pa) <= 1.1.

Iterative (N1)60cs with C_N = (Pa/sigma')^m, m = 0.784 - 0.0768 sqrt((N1)60cs).

``n1_60`` from other procedures is ignored; N60 is re-normalised here.
Returns ((N1)60cs, CRR7.5, dense mask (always False), converged).

Iterative q_c1Ncs with m = 1.338 - 0.249 q_c1Ncs^0.264 (q_c1Ncs limited to 21-254).

Uses q_t in place of q_c (Boulanger & Idriss recommend q_t where u2 is measured).
CSR = 0.65 (a_max/g) (sigma_v0 / sigma'_v0) r_d (Seed & Idriss 1971).

Stresses at the time of the earthquake.

With a profile, its seismic GWT is used unless ``gwt_depth`` overrides it. Without a
profile, ``gamma`` (e.g. estimated from the CPT) and ``gwt_depth`` are required.
Returns (sigma_v, u, sigma_v_eff, gwt_depth).
Top and bottom of the interval represented by each test point (midpoint rule).

LPI = integral over 0-20 m of F(z) w(z) dz (Iwasaki et al. 1978).

F = 1 - FS for FS < 1, else 0 (NaN FS, i.e. non-susceptible points, count as 0);
w = 10 - 0.5 z.

When the first test point is shallow (at most ``LPI_SURFACE_EXTENSION_DEPTH``), it also
represents the layer above it: its interval is extended up to the ground surface, where
the weight is largest (dropping that layer is on the unsafe side), but not above
``gwt_depth`` when given, since soil above the water table is not counted as liquefiable.
Iwasaki et al. (1982) categories.

Status per point. Order of precedence: excluded, above GWT, beyond depth, clay-like,
dense, invalid (no finite FS), then FS classes. FS is set to NaN for points without an FS.

r_d from Youd et al. (2001), Eq. (2), through 23 m.

The 23-30 m branch is the Robertson & Wride (1998) extension.
Depths greater than 30 m return NaN.

MSF. 'idriss': 10^2.24 / M^2.56 (lower bound of the NCEER range);
'andrus_stokoe': (M / 7.5)^-3.3 (upper bound, for M < 7.5).

K_sigma = (sigma'_v0 / Pa)^(f - 1), applied only for sigma'_v0 > Pa (K_sigma <= 1).

f = 0.7-0.8 for D_r 40-60 %, 0.6-0.7 for D_r 60-80 % (Youd et al. 2001).
(N1)60cs = alpha + beta (N1)60 (Idriss & Seed, in Youd et al. 2001 eqs. 6-7).
Returns ((N1)60cs, CRR7.5, dense mask). (N1)60 uses the Liao & Whitman C_N.

Iterative I_c following Youd et al. (2001), Eqs. (14)-(17).

Uses n = 1 (clay), 0.5 (sand), or 0.7 (intermediate), rather than
the intermediate exponent 0.75 of Robertson & Wride (1998).
Returns (Ic, n, F).

Grain characteristic correction K_c from Youd et al. (2001), Eq. (19).

Depends only on I_c. F is accepted for call compatibility and ignored;
the low-friction-ratio shortcut of Robertson & Wride (1998) is not used.
(R&W 1998 sets K_c = 1 for 1.64 < I_c < 2.36 with F < 0.5 %; it is absent from
Youd et al. 2001 Eq. 19. The surrounding PDF text was not verified.)
CRR7.5 from q_c1Ncs (Robertson & Wride 1998); NaN for q_c1Ncs >= 160.

Returns dict with qc1Ncs, CRR7.5, Ic, Kc, dense and clay-like masks.

Uses q_c (not q_t) as in Robertson & Wride (1998).

SPT-based triggering.

Parameters
----------
fc : fines content [%] per record (or one value for all). Required: there is no
    reliable default, so the assumption must be explicit.
pi : plasticity index [%] per record; PI >= 7 marks the point clay-like (NaN = unknown).
gwt_seismic : GWT during the earthquake; defaults to the profile's seismic GWT.
target_fs : user-defined required FS (typical 1.1-1.3); 1 <= FS < target is 'marginal'.
exclude : boolean mask of points the engineer marks non-liquefiable.

CPT-based triggering.

Without a profile, the unit weights estimated during processing are reused and
``gwt_seismic`` is required. For 'bi2014', FC defaults to the I_c estimate with ``c_fc``;
'youd2001' uses the K_c correction and ignores FC.

Process this layer's sources in ``[top, bottom)`` using the supplied profile.

Lab samples are independent depth points: no interpolation, nearest-sample
substitution, or replication of a PI measurement at every SPT depth. Numeric
raw lab fields are retained too, so changing a measured value changes the basis.
Soundings are cropped before processing, allowing them to extend below the profile.
Nonfinite processed inputs are absent rather than available to correlations.

One mean and depth spread per registry method, plus measured lab values.

Lab records supplied separately also provide registry inputs (e.g. PI). Exact
lab rows already emitted by ``layer_points`` are consumed once, not duplicated.
A PI correlation has source 'lab' but is not a direct lab measurement.
Prefer measurements, otherwise combine valid registry candidates only.

Resolve an explicit choice, revoking any previous approval on the copy.

Statistics use valid finite candidate representatives, with population standard
deviation (ddof=0). No mode means no engineer choice and raises ValueError.
Atomically resolve/approve requested choices and validate the resulting layer.
SHA-256 of bounds and the input multiset; ordering/bookkeeping do not matter.

Return refreshed candidates and suggestions without modifying project/design.

Stale selections retain selected/approved_at/basis_hash as the previous approval
trace, with approved=False. Approval requires matching inputs and dependent phi.

Process using Module 1, then propose without modifying the project.

SPT requires an existing unit-weight profile when tests are present, exactly
as Module 1 does; no bootstrap unit weight is invented. A log without tests
can be proposed without a profile. Missing logs fall back from spt_log to
spt_uscs_n, returning the effective settings and a warning for reproducibility.
Lab groups use the nearest sample within Module 1's existing LAB_MATCH_TOL
(an algorithmic matching distance); equal distances prefer the shallower
sample, then input order. ASTM D2487 classification is delegated unchanged to
classify_lab_record; incomplete or qualified classifications are flagged.
Existing processing messages are represented by a code, not copied as UI text.

Processing references (delegated, not reimplemented): Youd et al. (2001),
Table 2, N60 = N * (ER/60) * CB * CS * CR; Liao & Whitman (1986),
CN = sqrt(Pa/sigma_v_eff), with the existing NCEER cap of 1.7. CPT uses
Robertson (2009), iterative Qtn/Ic, and Robertson & Cabal (2010) unit weight
(see cpt_layers for the classification thresholds and gamma equation).

FC and PI per SPT record from the nearest lab sample within ``LAB_MATCH_TOL``.

Returns (fc, pi, notes). Records without lab FC use ``default_fc``; if that is None a
ValueError names the depths, because FC has no safe default.
Correct SPT records and normalise CPT soundings.

Hash the project inputs of a liquefaction run, including the profile selection.

``use_active`` is True when the run followed the project's active profile. Raises
``ValueError`` when the inputs contain non-finite numbers.
State of the liquefaction result stored in the project against its current inputs.
Process (if needed) and run the selected triggering method for every sounding.
Return {canonical name: column header} for the required and found optional columns.

Read a CPT(u) table; qc/fs/u2 are converted to kPa, depth to m.
